doc.title: Cal Collins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 11, 1997

title: Recording for Concord and Goodman's advice not to move to New York
summary: He worked in San Francisco for Concord but stayed in Cincinnati, as Goodman advised.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well you’ve been around the country, you’ve lived in a number of places. You moved to L.A. for a while, is that right?

No I didn’t, I didn’t live there, I just worked there in San Francisco, recording. That was when I was in the Concord years, when I was with Concord Jazz. And I did a lot of work out there and stayed there, two weeks at a time, that type of thing. But I’ve always been, I’ve always lived around that area, the Cincinnati area. I was planning on moving to New York, and Benny talked me out of it — Benny Goodman talked me out of it. He had said, “I hear you want to move to New York, and why” he says. I said, “Well that’s the thing to do.” He says, “Not anymore, not necessarily,” he says, “you live 35 minutes from an international airport in Cincinnati, and most of the gigs that you get, overseas and east coast and west coast, you get on an airplane and go, so why move to New York?” Talked me right out of it. I’m glad he did.
Yeah. Well he knew. He lived right there. How did that gig come about with him? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
